newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bomb injures 10 at police HQ in northern Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Bomb injures 10 at police HQ in northern Colombia.

text.p: A powerful bomb hidden in a street vendor's cart exploded outside a police headquarters in northwest Colombia on Monday, injuring at least 10 people, among them seven policemen, authorities said.
They said the injured included Col. Gabriel Antonio Carrero, commanding officer of the National Police in Monteria, capital of violence-torn Cordoba province.
Radio reports said the injury toll was closer to 30.
The bomb made of 88 pounds (40 kg) of dynamite was detonated by remote control.
Police said the blast shattered windows, damaging at least 17 buildings and many vehicles, and caused panic throughout the provincial capital.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility, but police said they suspected the attack was the work of Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels seeking to take reprisal for the demobilization over the weekend of more than 100 guerrillas from a rival rebel group.
An office responsible for parceling out land to rebels who lay down their arms is located just across the street from the police station where the bomb attack occurred.
Guerrillas and right-wing paramilitary groups have been fighting for years for control over rural areas of Cordoba and nearby Uraba, a banana-growing region near Colombia's border with Panama.
